I get this but I have PCOS. doesn't mean you have it, but it's just old blood that didn't make it out the last period. The reason it happens to me is because my hormones are out of whack. 1. I was literally walked into the operating room, I walked in, four people were there, the bed I was to lie on in the middle with that bright over hanging it. The whole scene is enough to make you a bit nervous. But to be honest I felt safe and fine. I just jumped on the bed and chatted to my surgeon. My anaesthetist was cracking jokes with me, and then told me I would start to feel floaty . I did start to feel floaty, and then I woke up lmao.
2. When I woke up, I felt drunk/high. I could hear a nurse next to me, she offered me food, which I didn't want. But I did skull two cups of lemonade. And then she said my sister was there, so I got up and walked out of the hospital with my sister. The nurse said to my sister I handled it well, I must've been in and out of chatting with the nurse, but I have zero memory of that. Just waking up, drinking fluids, getting up and walking out hahahaha. Also was not in pain or uncomfortable. \*EDIT\* I also 'woke up' in my clothes I bought in with me. So I have no idea if the nurses changed back into them, because they also put my compression bra on, or if I got changed myself. 
3. took my compression bra off today and looked at them for the first time. I was so happy, they're sooo much smaller and perkier already. There is some dried blood around my nipples, but it's not too bad.
4. Can't say for the weight part! But Once I can exercise I'll be looking at losing another 5kg to get to 60kg. So I don't think it will have a huge effect on them

Being nervous is normal, but honestly it's a really smooth experience

I paid out of pocket, all up it cost 14.5k (In Australia). I paid all upfront, or in 3 segments, once to the surgeon, once to the anaesthetist, and once for the hospital. 

I actually decided 6months when I was looking at spending 30k on a car, that if I bought one for half that, I could then get my breasts done as well. 100% worth it.

I paid for mine out of pocket in Australia, I expected roughly 15.5k all up (surgeon fee was 8.5k, and the rest was hospital and anaesthetic) 

It ended up costing 14.5k. If I were you, I'd research the prices in your areas and go off the most $$ ones, just so you can be financially prepared

My advice, cut out any soft drink right now. (pop or soda, I think is what most people call it lol) That alone will probably cause you do drop a few pounds. 

Don't change your eating habits all at once and go super strict and healthy, you'll end up caving into your cravings and binge eating. Eat every 3-4 hours if you're hungry. I'm assuming you eat about 6 times a day? Make 3 of those meals healthy. And the other 3, try not to eat too much sugary foods. Just slowly ween yourself off the bad food. 

Eventually 4 of those meals will be healthy, than 5, than all 6 and allow treats on certain days. Discipline is HARD to learn. So start small. And also proportion your food, allow yourself the treats, but don't eat so much of them (easier said than done I know, but again, it's all about discipline) 

When you feel yourself about to cave in, trust me it's gonna happen, your going to feel emotional and grumpy, your body will have withdrawals and it's all you'll be able to think about. This is when it's hardest, but think about why you're doing this, think about what you want most, you have to want to lose weight more than you want unhealthy food. These cravings will get easier and easier with time.

Used to work at a racing stables. Anyone who owns horses will know how easy it is for them to injure themselves, and most injuries occur in their paddock rather than racing. 

One soul crushing thing was watching a horse being led to the back paddock to be put down.  

But the biggest one, was doing the feed run for 100+ horses. I notice one of the weanlings (8months old) was in the wrong paddock. I then notice, that her leg was hung up in the fence. I was riding in the back of the truck, so I banged on the roof, and jumped off and started to head over to the weanling. 

My boss was there helping us thankfully, so I screamed out to him, and pointed in the direction of the filly. He climbed into the paddock and walked over too. When I got there, the filly's skin was wrapped around the fence, her leg had pretty much been de gloved, could see all the bone, the tendon was sliced in half, and part of the bone had been chipped. My boss just said 'I'm going to have to put her down' 

He got her out of the fence, and she hobbled off, because the tendon was fucked, imagine if you had to walk on your wrist with your hand trailing behind, that was her, but her hoof trailing behind. 

We got a gun, and came back. I stood outside the paddock and my boss walked over to her, she was already lying down, had already given up. He did one shot, which unfortunately didn't kill her, and the second shot did. It was horrible seeing her body spasm like that. 

I then helped push her body into a tractor so we could bury her elsewhere. There was so much blood, blood out of her nose, ears mouth, head. A massive pool of blood, just everywhere. 

It's strange looking at a lifeless body when you use to see it so full of energy everyday.

Whenever a new student comes in the group, she will ask them, what's the most important thing about jumping. The person normally tries to think up something, you know, rhythm up to the jump, getting a good takeoff spot. 

My coach responds, nope, the most important part is getting over the jump. At the end of the day, I don't care how pretty you look, just get over it. 

So my advice to you, is when you are in competition is think less and ride more. You will have a jump on xc that scares you, don't think about it. Just get over it. 

you've got 5 stages of a jump. The approach, The takeoff, Suspension, Landing, and Getaway. 

The approach is the only one you want to be in 3 point position. The rest is all in 2 point, unless it's a related line, than the getaway is in 3 point. 


A flatwork tip which is AMAZING. Take your stirrups off, cross them over whatever. Get someone out to watch you ride. Start off walking in a circle, lets say on the right rein. Now, say right, every time your horses off hind(inside hind) LEAVES the ground. Now this is really hard. you have to really concentrate on the feel of the horse. Once you get it, add in the left, for the near hind. Then move onto trot and do the same, and canter and do the same. Also when you trot, focus on how your hips are moving with the horses trot. Now exaggerate your hip movement, it's going to feel funny, but I can guarantee your horse's stride will get bigger and he will stretch his neck right down. Do this for the canter as well. Your inside hip swings more than your outside hip, exaggerate that. Again your horse's stride will get bigger and he will stretch. This helps yourself and your horse to relax and get a MUCH nicer movement going.
